definition: Andrew William Moore is a British-American computer scientist whose research spans machine learning, artificial intelligence, robotics, and large-scale statistical data mining.
details: He is the co-founder and CEO of Lovelace AI, a Pittsburgh-based technology company. Moore previously served as Dean of the Carnegie Mellon School of Computer Science from 2014 to 2018 and held senior roles at Google, including leading Google Cloud AI. In 2023, he was appointed the first adviser for artificial intelligence, robotics, and cloud computing to the United States Central Command.

explainer.lead: Andrew W. Moore is a British-American computer scientist.

contributions.name: He founded the Auton Laboratory, which focused on large-scale statistical methods, and co-founded a consultancy applying statistical data mining to manufacturing problems.

A key aspect of Moore's contributions lies in developing scalable techniques for statistical data mining and computational statistics, particularly through the founding of the Auton Lab at Carnegie Mellon University in 1993.
To disseminate knowledge in these fields, Moore created extensive online tutorials covering foundational and advanced topics in statistical machine learning and big data.

timeline.what: His 1991 thesis, titled Efficient Memory-based Learning for Robot Control, was supervised by William F. Clocksin and examined machine learning techniques applied to robot control.

=== Carnegie Mellon University faculty (1993–2006) === Moore joined the Carnegie Mellon University faculty in 1993 as an assistant professor in machine learning, reinforcement learning, manufacturing, and non-parametric regression.
He received tenure in 2000 and held appointments in the Computer Science Department, the Machine Learning Department, and the Robotics Institute.
He left Carnegie Mellon in 2006 to join Google.
Moore was appointed Dean of the Carnegie Mellon School of Computer Science in April 2014, succeeding Randal Bryant, who had held the role since 2004, and took up the position in August of that year.
